Choose the structure that matches your scientific question. Use this overview
when observations, species, individuals, sites, or lines are not independent
after the fixed effects have been included and you need a structured random
effect instead of an ordinary random intercept.

This overview assumes you have already fit and interpreted a plain
location-scale model, for example the Gaussian tutorial in
[When variance carries signal, Part 1](location-scale.html), and now need one of the
structured layers below because your observations are grouped, related, or
spatially structured.

In `drmTMB`, a structural-dependence term is a latent random effect with a known
relationship structure. It is separate from residual coscale `rho12`, which is
the within-observation residual correlation between two responses. Use
`corpairs()` for fitted latent random-effect correlations and `rho12()` for
fitted residual response-response correlations.

## Pick the route

| Your question | A sensible starting point | What to check before reporting | Read next |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Do related individuals share additive genetic deviations, such as heritable trait differences? | `animal(1 | individual, pedigree = pedigree)`, `animal(1 | individual, A = A)`, or `animal(1 | individual, Ainv = Ainv)` | Fitted for the documented Gaussian `mu`/`sigma`, slope, q2, and q4 routes. The supported non-Gaussian models fit ordinary Poisson/NB2 q1 animal `mu` intercept-plus-one-slope, NB2 q1 animal `sigma` (run `check_drm()` and read the guide before reporting it), and the beta animal models described in the guide. Assembling the pedigree or `Ainv` relatedness matrix automatically, sparse large-pedigree construction, additional multiple or labelled slope layouts outside the documented fitted models, and non-Gaussian neighbours outside those models are not available yet. | [Animal models and additive relatedness](animal-models.html) |
| Do related species share evolutionary deviations? | `phylo(1 | species, tree = tree)` | Fitted for the documented Gaussian `mu`/`sigma`, slope, q2/q4, direct-SD, and `corpair()` routes. The supported non-Gaussian models fit ordinary Poisson/NB2 q1 phylogenetic `mu` intercept-plus-one-slope and NB2 q1 phylogenetic `sigma` (run `check_drm()` and read the guide before reporting it); Student-t q1 phylogenetic `nu` is diagnostic-only, while cumulative-logit q1 phylogenetic `mu` is diagnostic-only. Neighbouring non-Gaussian routes are not available yet. | [Phylogenetic structured effects](phylogenetic-models.html) |
| Do nearby sites share smooth deviations, either through coordinates or a smooth field fitted from a mesh? | `spatial(1 | site, coords = coords)`, `spatial(1 + depth | site, coords = coords)`, or `spatial(1 | site, mesh = mesh)` for a mesh-based option with a fixed spatial range | Fitted for the documented coordinate-spatial Gaussian `mu`/`sigma`, slope, q2, and q4 routes. The separate mesh route is only `bf(y ~ spatial(1 | site, mesh = mesh), sigma ~ 1)` for a projected-coordinate, fixed-kappa Gaussian `mu` intercept at local-fit level. The supported non-Gaussian models fit ordinary Poisson/NB2 q1 spatial `mu` intercept-plus-one-slope and NB2 q1 spatial `sigma` (run `check_drm()` and read the guide before reporting it); Student-t q1 spatial `mu` is diagnostic-only for the intercept and has only a preliminary check for the intercept-plus-one-slope route. All three spatial-inflation models (Poisson `zi`, fixed-`zi` Poisson `mu`, and fixed-`zi` NB2 `mu`) are diagnostic-only routes checked on a single example. Mesh slopes/range and other mesh fields, additional multiple or labelled coordinate-slope layouts outside the documented fitted models, non-Gaussian routes outside those exact models, and spatial `corpair()` routes are not available yet. | [Coordinate-spatial structured effects](spatial-models.html) |
| Does the same response need both species and site structure at once? | Fit separate `phylo()` and `spatial()` models for now | A combined route is not available yet; simultaneous structural layers need their own identifiability checks before use. | [Structural dependence tutorial](https://itchyshin.github.io/drmTMB/articles/phylogenetic-spatial.html) |
| Is the known matrix neither a pedigree, species tree, nor spatial coordinate surface? | `relmat(1 | id, K = K)` or `relmat(1 | id, Q = Q)` | Fitted for the documented Gaussian `mu`/`sigma`, slope, q2, and q4 routes. The supported non-Gaussian models fit ordinary Poisson/NB2 q1 relmat `mu` intercept-plus-one-slope, NB2 q1 relmat `sigma` (run `check_drm()` and read the guide before reporting it), Gamma q1 relmat `mu`, and truncated-NB2 q1 relmat `hu`. Additional multiple or labelled slope layouts outside the documented fitted models, broader K/Q bridge claims, predictor-dependent `corpair()` routes, and non-Gaussian neighbours outside those models are not available yet. | [Known-matrix relatedness with relmat](relmat-known-matrices.html) |

## What to read next

Read the detailed [structural-dependence tutorial](https://itchyshin.github.io/drmTMB/articles/phylogenetic-spatial.html)
when you need fitted examples, equations, diagnostics, and interval guidance.
That article is still the detailed page for animal, phylogenetic, spatial,
combined-layer, and `relmat()` material while the topic is being split into
smaller articles.

Read [animal models and additive relatedness](animal-models.html) when your
first question is specifically about `animal()`, `pedigree`, `A`, or `Ainv`.
Read [phylogenetic structured effects](phylogenetic-models.html) when your
first question is specifically about `phylo()`, tree-based covariance,
`sd_phylo*()`, or phylogenetic `corpair()` rows.
Read [two-tree phylogenetic interactions](bipartite-phylogenetic-interactions.html)
when one observation belongs to a pair of partner species drawn from two
phylogenies, such as plant-pollinator or host-parasite pairs.
Read [coordinate-spatial structured effects](spatial-models.html) when your
first question is specifically about `spatial()`, site coordinates,
coordinate-spatial slopes, spatial q=2 `corpairs()` rows, or the constant
spatial q=4 location-scale block.
Read [known-matrix relatedness with relmat](relmat-known-matrices.html) when
the matrix is a lower-level latent covariance or precision matrix that does not
belong to the animal, phylogenetic, or spatial routes.

Read the [formula grammar](formula-grammar.html) when you want the compact
implemented-versus-planned syntax table. Read the
[figure gallery](https://itchyshin.github.io/drmTMB/articles/figure-gallery.html) when you want to see how `rho12`,
ordinary group, phylogenetic, spatial, animal-model, and `relmat()` correlation
rows should stay visually separate.

## Fitted versus planned

A successful fit does not show that every related model is reliable. Each row
in the table above names the exact combination of family, mean, residual
scale, and correlation structure that has a worked example and its own checks.
A model that looks similar but changes one of those pieces, a different
family, an extra slope, or a combined structure, needs its own check before
you trust its numbers: start with `check_drm()` and the guide the route links
to.

The fitted first slices are useful for applied work, but they are not full
parity across every structural layer. Fitting matching structured terms in two
response means links those two traits through one shared structured
correlation. Adding matching structured terms to all four pieces of a
model, both means and both residual scales, links them through one
four-parameter structured block for constant location-scale covariance. The
univariate intercept route can also enter `sigma` for `phylo()`, `spatial()`,
`animal()`, and `relmat()`. A one-slope `sigma` route also fits for all four
structures: for `phylo()`, `animal()` with an additive relatedness matrix, and
`relmat()` with `K` or `Q`, that route has an interval you can report, with
caveats explained in each guide; for `spatial()`, you can fit and inspect the
estimate, but do not report an interval for it yet. None of this implies
multiple or labelled structured slopes, non-Gaussian structural effects
outside the exact model-specific support named above, or predictor-dependent
`corpair()` regressions unless the route table explicitly names that support.

Known sampling covariance belongs to the meta-analysis route, not `relmat()`.
Use `relmat()` for latent random-effect relatedness matrices; use
`meta_V(V = V)` and the [meta-analysis documentation](meta-analysis.html)
when the covariance matrix describes known observation-level sampling error.

With one or more structured fits in hand, the next stage in the reader path is
checking whether they are trustworthy and comparing candidates: continue with
[Model selection with AIC and BIC](model-selection.html).
